profile.name: Nisarg Shah
profile.description: Building data-driven solutions through statistical analysis, machine learning, and large-scale data processing, while exploring cloud, MLOps, and AI engineering.

featuredProjects.title: Uniswap V3 LP Position Profitability Prediction
featuredProjects.description: Predicts whether a Uniswap V3 liquidity position will be profitable at the moment it is opened, providing data-driven guidance on concentrated price-range selection. Built a leakage-safe ML pipeline on 62,250 closed positions extracted from 9 on-chain data sources across the highest-volume pools, with custom feature engineering for tick ranges, fee events, and partial withdrawal handling. Logistic Regression and XGBoost were evaluated with chronological train/test splitting to prevent temporal leakage, and SHAP was used to interpret predictions. A key finding was that positions whose ranges did not overlap the pool's recently traded price range were profitable only 23% of the time, compared with 60% when they did.

featuredProjects.title: Criteo CTR Prediction
featuredProjects.description: Implemented and benchmarked the same click-through-rate prediction workflow across three computing environments: a Docker-based PySpark cluster, an AWS EC2 Spark cluster, and single-machine scikit-learn. Built preprocessing pipelines for the Criteo 1M dataset handling median imputation, log transformations, feature hashing for high-cardinality categoricals, and sparse feature assembly. Trained Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient-Boosted Trees models with 2-fold cross-validation. The best model achieved a 0.537 PR-AUC against a 25.5% positive-class baseline, with benchmarks comparing execution characteristics across the single-machine and distributed setups.

featuredProjects.title: Debunking the Left-Right Batting Advantage
featuredProjects.description: Contributed to an independent-study analysis investigating whether left-right batting partnerships are inherently more effective than same-handed combinations in international Test cricket. The study processed ball-by-ball data from 750+ Test matches (2002–2022) covering over 1.5 million deliveries, reconstructing partnerships by iterating deliveries and accumulating runs until a dismissal before tagging each pair as left-left, right-right, or left-right. Because player names differed across the two source datasets, the team combined them with a fuzzy matching algorithm that reached 96% matching accuracy. Three hypotheses were tested: partnership batting averages, total runs, and strike rates across combinations; a restricted view using only the top seven partnerships per match to reduce lower-order influence; and a strike-change analysis of runs and dismissals on the delivery immediately following a change of strike (200,000+ strike changes, 100,000+ runs, and nearly 4,000 dismissals). In every view the differences between left-right and same-handed combinations were too small to establish a meaningful advantage, so the analysis did not support the hypothesis.

allProjects.title: Navicore
allProjects.description: A multimodal, GPS-style route finder for Mumbai's transport network: it models the city's suburban rail and bus networks as a single weighted graph built from stops, routes, and schedule data, then runs shortest-path search to surface the best rail + bus route between any two landmarks. Built in Python with NetworkX and shipped through an interactive web front end (Next.js, TypeScript, D3.js) with a live Streamlit deployment — so instead of guessing on the platform, you get the actual shortest path that mixes trains and buses.

allProjects.title: IPL Fantasy League Dashboard
allProjects.description: An auction-based fantasy cricket league, automated end-to-end. The app scrapes live match data as games unfold, converts every player's performance into fantasy points using a role-based scoring rulebook, and streams a live leaderboard to a Streamlit dashboard. An auction module handles squad drafting ahead of the season, and standings keep refreshing as each match progresses — the fantasy league's answer to a post-match command centre, without a manual spreadsheet in sight.

allProjects.title: PAT.ai: Data Analysis Assistant
allProjects.description: Wish you could explore a dataset without writing pandas code? PAT.ai is a Streamlit-based data analysis assistant that turns plain-English questions into real analytics. Type something like 'how does revenue vary by region?', and the app maps your query to a predefined analytical workflow, runs the statistical analysis quietly in the background, and returns a clean Plotly chart. It's a fast, conversational on-ramp to exploratory data analysis for anyone who wants answers, not syntax.
